name: kiln-and-cup

subject.name: Kiln & Cup
subject.audience: Buyers of handmade tableware who choose a one-of-a-kind piece from photographs alone
subject.primaryJob: Let a buyer trust how a single wood-fired piece will look and feel in the hand before buying it
sources: Wood-fired stoneware: ash glaze runs, flashing and iron spots left by the flame
The kiln and its fuel: stacked wood, ash, clay wadding marks
Glazes the studio uses: iron tenmoku, ash celadon, unglazed clay body

principles: Beauty in everyday objects, honest making
Imperfection and use as part of the form
Departs: not a Japanese brand, so no brush lettering, no indigo-and-kraft, no Japanese motifs

territories.name: Kiln yard
territories.description: The studio after a firing: pots cooling on wooden boards, ash on every surface, raking daylight that shows glaze depth and the texture of the clay.
territories.light: soft raking daylight from one side, so surfaces read
territories.textures: real glaze and clay in photographs only; no faked texture in the interface
territories.composition: one piece per frame, generous room around it
territories.imagery: close photographs of each piece in hand and on a board, true color

muse.name: Lucie Rie
muse.take: Restraint and precision: thin, exact edges and surfaces that let the glaze speak
muse.leave: Her forms and sgraffito lines as motifs; no imitation of her pots or her name as styling

signature.reason: Every piece is one of a kind; airy space gives each photograph the room a single pot gets on a bare board in the kiln yard

rationale.form.space: Airy, as the signature: one piece per view with room to look at it
rationale.form.elevation: Flat: pieces sit on the page as pots sit on a board; shadows belong to the photographs, not the interface
rationale.form.line: Hairline: the workshop's pencil-label line, echoing Rie's thin exact edges
rationale.color.character.vibrancy: Muted: glaze and clay colors are earthy, and the interface must not out-color the photographs
rationale.movement: Calm: warm and plain, no hard sell
rationale.adaptivity: Light-first: buyers judge glaze color against a daylight page
rationale.color.anchors.0: Tenmoku iron glaze as the dark main solid, not terracotta
rationale.grounding.primary: Mingei reinterpreted: its values without Japanese styling

samples.action: Add this cup to your basket
samples.confirmation: It's yours. We'll wrap it and send it this week.
samples.error: That piece has just sold. Each one is made once, so here are others from the same firing.

avoid: Brush lettering or any faux-Japanese calligraphy
Indigo and kraft paper as a default palette
Warm cream with a serif and terracotta accents
Urgency and scarcity sales copy (countdowns, 'only 1 left!')
